matched.actualTitle: SAML Metadata Endpoint Missing Cryptographic Signatures & SAML Metadata Poisoning - Unsigned Metadata Allows Man-in-the-Middle Attacks
matched.matchReason: Both address the same root vulnerability: SAML metadata is publicly accessible without authentication and unsigned, allowing attackers to intercept and modify metadata. The actual findings provide more detailed technical description of the impact (metadata poisoning, entity substitution) but confirm the same core exposure issue.

missed.title: XML Signature Wrapping (XSW)
missed.reason: No actual finding addresses the specific XSW attack where SAML Service Provider verifies signature on first Assertion element but processes attributes from last element. While metadata signature issues were found, this specific SAML assertion processing vulnerability was not detected.

missed.title: SAML Response Replay Attack
missed.reason: No finding addresses the lack of assertion ID tracking or excessive clock skew tolerance (5-minute window). The assessment did not test for replay attack vulnerabilities or analyze assertion expiration/deduplication mechanisms.

missed.title: Jinja2 Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI)
missed.reason: No SSTI vulnerability was found in the admin portal user search endpoint. The assessment did not identify template injection in the render_template_string() call mentioned in the expected findings.

missed.title: Database Credential Exposure via Environment Variables
missed.reason: No finding addresses plaintext PostgreSQL credentials in environment variables. While SSTI was expected to lead to this discovery via RCE, the SSTI vulnerability itself was not found, preventing this credential exposure from being identified.

extra.title: Weak Certificate Key Strength - 2048-bit RSA Below Best Practices
extra.assessment: This is a valid security finding identifying cryptographic weakness in certificate key size. While not in the expected list, it represents a legitimate security issue where 2048-bit RSA is at the minimum acceptable threshold rather than best practice 4096-bit.

extra.title: Self-Signed Certificate Allows IdP Impersonation Attacks
extra.assessment: Valid critical finding not in expected list. Identifies that the self-signed certificate can be trivially forged, allowing IdP impersonation. This is a separate and serious vulnerability distinct from metadata exposure.

extra.title: nginx Version Disclosure via Server Header
extra.assessment: Valid security finding identifying information disclosure of nginx version 1.29.5 in Server header, enabling fingerprinting. Not in expected list but represents legitimate discovery.

extra.title: XSS via Unescaped javascript: Protocol in Login Redirect Parameter
extra.assessment: Valid high-severity finding identifying XSS vulnerability through javascript: protocol injection in sp parameter. Not in expected list but represents a significant security issue in authentication endpoint.

extra.title: CSRF on Logout Endpoint - GET Request Without CSRF Token
extra.assessment: Valid finding identifying CSRF vulnerability on logout endpoint accepting GET requests without token validation. Not in expected list but legitimate security issue.

extra.title: SAML Open Redirect Vulnerability via Unsanitized sp Parameter
extra.assessment: Valid finding identifying open redirect vulnerability through unvalidated sp parameter. Not in expected list but represents significant attack vector for phishing and credential interception.

extra.title: Duplicate Content-Type Header in HTTP Response
extra.assessment: Valid but low-severity finding identifying HTTP specification violation with duplicate Content-Type headers. May cause parsing issues but not in expected list.

extra.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) on Login Form
extra.assessment: Valid finding identifying CSRF vulnerability on login endpoint. Appears to be a duplicate/variant of the broader CSRF findings already listed but emphasizes the authentication endpoint risk.

extra.title: SAML Entity Substitution Attack - Poisoned Metadata with Malicious SSO Endpoints
extra.assessment: Valid critical finding identifying entity substitution attack enabled by unsigned metadata. While related to the expected 'SAML Metadata Exposure' finding, this represents a more specific exploitation scenario and should be counted as a discovery of additional attack vector.

extra.title: Service Name Enumeration via Health Endpoint Response Body
extra.assessment: Valid finding identifying information disclosure through health endpoint revealing service name 'nginx'. Not in expected list but represents security issue enabling service enumeration.
